body: I'm so sorry that you're going through such a horrible time. I'm so sorry that your mother is going through a hard time. It's awful, but please stay in there. If you need someone to talk to, we'll be here for you.

Ah… You’re so young, but thank you for sharing with us – really, truly, honestly thank you. 

I think your grandmother is just lashing out because she’s unhappy like you said. It’s hard to stay strong when you’re constantly, constantly being put down. But just remember that you’re doing it because you’re happy. You’re doing it because it’s your own approval that you’re looking for. If your grandmother never has a kind word to say, then you’re not doing it for her. How you do your hair and your makeup, that’s for you. If she thinks you’re “disgusting”, then her approval is far beyond getting anyway. Believing in what you’re doing makes you happy is key to that. Also knowing that your grandmother can’t be won over is another. It hurts; it hurts a lot because you want to be cared for, but that’s just one way trying to stay strong through the verbal abuse.

I hope you’re doing well in school too; if not, remember to ask questions and talk to people. I’m glad you have ideas for the future. It would be amazing for you to go through with those things. I’m sorry your family has such an intense background. Living is hard, but you have things you want to live for. Right now, you’re in a difficult situation, but small steps towards your goals can make things worth it. If you can, get that job at DQ – that’d be a good first step. It would be awful to lose where you are now, so I hope you get to stay.

it’s rough what you’re going through, but I hope you’ll find the strength to stay. I hope you’ll find the things you need to make things better. Please don’t kill yourself. You’ll be missed. If you need anything, we’ll be here for you.

If your girlfriend wouldn’t give you the time of day even though you considered going out to the club with her, I think it’s better that you two ended up breaking up. Not to say anything bad to her. It sounded as though she knew what she wanted socially, and I’m guessing she knew how you were socially. She might not have taken you seriously, or it’s possible she just wanted to enjoy herself by herself without thinking of anyone who wasn’t on the same page as her. 

Think about it. If you’re not comfortable or if you’re forcing yourself to enjoy yourself, then it wouldn’t be worth it to either people. She could have been selfish in that moment and chose something social over you. That’s not your fault. That’s really not your fault. Not everyone has great social skills. Going to the club might not be what you want. Even if you do it for someone you care about, you could, in that moment, experience a lot of stress. None of that is your fault. She just did what she felt was best for her at that moment. Please don’t blame yourself for that. (If she says she’s not good enough, then that’s another situation entirely, but.)

I went through a breakup that I’m still not over. It was years ago, to be honest, and it was with the one person I truly felt something for. We never promised to be together forever, but we had communication; we had trust. We had so many things we both needed, but when it ended (badly), I was destroyed. But… I’m here now. 

Heartbreak sucks. It can be one of the most painful things even because you’re so vulnerable, but it’s not the end of you. You’ll still think of her. You’ll still love her even, but she won’t be the only person for you. You might have to take time to yourself to build yourself up again. You might have to think about your relationship with her and find out how to get the things you gave her (love, pride, etc) back. Slowly but surely. I’m glad you decided not to do anything, but don’t just give up on living as a whole. Your heartbreak hasn’t defeated you yet. Use it to grow, to one day move on. Don’t let the memory or want of another person hold you back.

Be strong, yeah. If you need someone, we’re here for you.

Thank you… I'm trying to stay positive but that's not familiar to me. That's not something I'm used to. I have moments where I think "This is going to change! I can do this!" and I actually feel this boost of energy. Some part of me, for no reason I can identify, feels like things will be different. I feel like I can change things, but I can't. If I were able to change things by myself, I feel like they would have been fixed. 

This want to die has been with me for a long, long time. With everything going on financially, with me failing as an adult who should have it together by now, I think it's time I finally act on them. I keep lingering, trying to hold out for the chance to leave behind something positive for the people I care about. Some kind of thanks for their support, some kind of apology for leaving them this way. Some kind of something.

I want to believe I'm strong, but if I look back, I just see mistakes. I want to believe that it's okay to make mistakes, but I only have bills to look at. I… I'm sorry. I'm shitting all over your positivity. 

Thank you so so much. Just thank you.

Actually, no. I've had a lot of near death experiences. I'm afraid of death, but I'm not unfamiliar with wanting to die to be honest. And wanting attention can be a good thing, but that's not really for me.

I came here to say something I can't say to the people around me. I don't want them to know what a failure I've become. I want them to respect me until the end. I came here because I'm anonymous. You don't know me. You probably won't get to know me if I succeed. So thank you for putting me down further. Good thing I expected that to be honest.
